About me

Aaron
Shan.

I am currently a student at Burnaby North Secondary, and I love helping out around my community through school activities, events, and student-led projects. I enjoy swimming, debate, coding, poster and website design, public speaking, and business competitions. It’s nice to meet you.

Tutoring / Non-Profit

Electrical Engineering Tutor

Non-Profit STEM Outreach

Designed and delivered engaging, hands-on introductory electrical engineering and electronics lessons to students through a youth-led STEM outreach platform.

View project details

Making engineering approachable.

I translated concepts such as circuits, currents, switches, and basic hardware into interactive lessons designed for younger learners.

  • Taught more than 9 one-hour classes.
  • Spent over 12 hours preparing and delivering lessons.
  • Used project-based activities to help students learn by building.
Visual Design

Grade 10 Council Website

Official Student Council Hub

Created an official online hub for the Grade 10 Council to share events, fundraisers, FAQs, and student recruitment information.

View project details

A central hub for the student body.

The website was designed as a modern touchpoint between student council and Grade 10 students.

  • Included events, news, FAQ, recruitment, and team sections.
  • Focused on clarity, simple navigation, and a bold school-focused visual style.
  • Designed around representation, fundraising, and school events.
UI / Social Media

Social Media Manager

3+ Student Accounts

Managed social media content for student council and school clubs to promote events, transit advocacy, fundraisers, and student engagement.

View project details

Turning updates into content students notice.

Traditional announcements can be missed easily. I created content that made school initiatives easier to understand and more interesting to follow.

  • Created event posters, club updates, and recruitment graphics.
  • Managed content for Grade 10 Council, TNC, and NEGC.
  • Supported fundraisers, transit advocacy, and school involvement.
